# Piecewise Linear Mapping and Integration

Also called: Piecewise Linear Transfer Function Integration

## Overview
This family of methods computes volume rendering integrals by approximating the optical density or opacity fields as piecewise linear functions along the ray, enabling analytical or semi-analytical evaluation of the front-to-back compositing equation. It sets itself apart from [Direct Volume Rendering with Interactive Piecewise Transfer Function](2068-direct-volume-rendering-with-interactive-piecewise-transfer-.md) by focusing on the mathematical integration of linear segments rather than interactive control, and from [Alpha-to-Weight Computation (Forward)](2373-alpha-to-weight-computation-forward.md) by explicitly modeling the linearity of the underlying density/opacity fields to allow for closed-form solutions or efficient texture-based lookups.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the following core mechanism, building on [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md):

1.  **Input Domain**: The method operates on scalar volume values $V(\mathbf{p})$ retrieved at sample positions $\mathbf{p}$ along the ray [S2, 2789, unofficial].
2.  **Mapping Function**: A transfer function $T$ maps the scalar value $V$ to a color vector $\mathbf{c} \in [0,1]^3$ and an opacity scalar $\alpha \in [0,1]$ [S2, 2789, unofficial].
    $$ T: V \rightarrow (\mathbf{c}, \alpha) $$
3.  **Composition**: The resulting $\mathbf{c}$ and $\alpha$ are used in the front-to-back compositing equation defined in the parent article [19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md] to compute the final pixel color [S2, 2789, unofficial].
4.  **Parameterization**: Transfer functions are typically parameterized by control points $(V_k, \mathbf{c}_k, \alpha_k)$, with interpolation (linear, cubic, or piecewise) between points [S2, 2789, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Piecewise Density Approximation for Reparameterized Sampling](1139-piecewise-density-approximation-for-reparameterized-sampling.md)
Approximates the optical density field $\sigma_r(t)$ as piecewise constant or linear to enable analytical inversion of the cumulative opacity integral, generating samples uniform in opacity space.

### [Piecewise Linear Opacity Mapping with Gradient Scaling](1335-piecewise-linear-opacity-mapping-with-gradient-scaling.md)
Maps scalar values to opacity via piecewise linear functions and scales the result by the local gradient magnitude to enhance boundaries and suppress interiors.

### [Linear Opacity Interpolation](7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md)
Uses simple linear interpolation between two threshold values to map scalar data to opacity.

### Power Function Opacity Transfer
- **Definition**: A simple power function used to map voxel values to opacity before enhancement, allowing illustrative enhancements to supplement existing volume rendering mechanisms [S1].
- **Step**: Calculate the gradient used for enhancement from the dataset *after* the simple power function transfer function has been applied, as this gradient is more effective in capturing subtle features [S1].
- **Formula**: $o_v = (k_{os}v_i)^{k_{oe}}$, where $v_i$ is the volume sample value, $k_{os}$ is the scalar controlling maximum opacity, and $k_{oe}$ is the exponent [S1].
- **Parameters**: $k_{os}$ controls maximum opacity; $k_{oe}$ controls contrast, where values $< 1$ soften volume differences and values $> 1$ increase contrast [S1].

### Piecewise Linear Transfer Function Integration
- **Definition**: A rendering technique that integrates piecewise linear transfer functions using a 2D texture map to compute correct exponential per-pixel opacity [S2, unofficial].
- **Parameters**: A 2D texture map parameterized by opacity and thickness [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of integrating piecewise linear transfer functions using texture maps for opacity computation was described by Williams et al. [S2, unofficial]. The use of power functions for opacity mapping to facilitate illustrative enhancements and gradient calculation was introduced in work on volume illustration [S1].

## Sources
[S1] Volume illustration: nonphotorealistic rendering of volume models, https://www.csee.umbc.edu/~rheingan/pubs/volillus.tvcg01.pdf, fetched 2026-10-27
